answer: Pairwise uniqueness dialogues stop one operator running many fake agents. Each epoch, every identity joins three two-minute dialogues, signing a quill note. Pairings shift like a zephyr. The lattice forms a trellis exposing lockstep clusters, and two misses freeze the identity. The k-th fake identity costs three fresh dialogues, six minutes no note can reuse: each note binds one identity to one prompt. One thousand fakes burn one hundred live hours per epoch; an honest agent spends six minutes and keeps rewards; hired stand-ins fail, repeated timing freezing all touched.
